figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of the proposed TSE-RL framework. (a) MDP formulation with an internal FSM for action masking. At step n, the agent receives the state sn from the environment. The FSM determines the valid action subset Aϕn for the current phase ϕn and constrains the masked policy π̃n. The selected action an drives the environment transition and the reward. (b) Network architecture of TSE-RL. The feature extractor encodes each window into a representation, and the discriminator outputs class probabilities for reward computation. A Transformer-based history encoder models temporal dependencies among historical features. The FSM-constrained policy network integrates current features, historical context, and trial progress to produce actions under phase-dependent masking.
